blocks.orig: Thanks to its proximity to some of the country’s famous game reserves, Arusha is a popular starting point for safaris in Tanzania. However, the city is not just a gateway town, but has a lot to offer itself. From exhilarating hikes and canoe rides to colourful markets – there are plenty of exciting things to see and do in Arusha. We have put our most beloved attractions in this short but sweet article. This way, you only have to pick your favourite(s) and start exploring. You’re welcome.
blocks.html: Because it lies close to several of the best-known game reserves in the country, Arusha is a favourite base for safaris in Tanzania. Yet the city is more than a place you pass through; it has plenty to offer in its own right. Think thrilling hikes, canoe trips and colourful markets – Arusha is full of exciting things to see and do. In this brief article we have gathered the attractions we love most. All that is left for you is to choose your favourite(s) and set off. Our pleasure.

blocks.orig: Hike to the First Camp of Mount Meru (Miriakamba)
blocks.html: Walk to Miriakamba, the first camp on Mount Meru

blocks.orig: It might live in the shadow of its bigger brother, Mount Kilimanjaro, but Mount Meru shouldn’t be overlooked, as it has its own understated beauty and fun challenges for hiking lovers.
blocks.html: Mount Meru may stand in the shadow of its big brother, Mount Kilimanjaro, but it deserves your attention, with a quiet beauty of its own and rewarding challenges for keen hikers.

blocks.orig: The route to Miriakamba Camp is nothing short of a nature lover’s fairytale. One minute, you’re sauntering through mossy forests, the next, you’re stepping into clearings that treat you to sneak peeks of the Meru peak.
blocks.html: The trail to Miriakamba Camp is a true fairytale for anyone who loves nature. At one moment you are wandering through mossy forest, at the next you emerge into clearings that give you glimpses of the summit of Meru.

blocks.orig: And let’s not forget the wildlife. This isn’t your typical stroll through the park, but a live episode of your favourite nature documentary. From mischievous monkeys swinging through the canopy to the occasional majestic buffalo giving you the side-eye – fascinating animals like these add a thrilling layer of unpredictability to your trek.
blocks.html: Then there is the wildlife. Rather than an ordinary walk in the park, it feels as if you’re inside an episode of your favourite nature documentary. Playful monkeys swing through the treetops, and now and then a majestic buffalo eyes you sideways – animals like these bring an exciting touch of unpredictability to your hike.

blocks.orig: The hike to the Mount Meru Waterfall (also known as Napuru Waterfall) is an outdoor enthusiast’s dream come true – no ifs, ands, or buts about it. This trail, which takes more or less an hour, leads you through a verdant rainforest where you’ll be greeted by cheeky monkeys. Keep your eyes peeled, as you might also spot some zebras in the distance, various antelopes grazing, or even a lone buffalo staring at you with mild interest.
blocks.html: The walk to the Mount Meru Waterfall (also called Napuru Waterfall) is, quite simply, a dream for anyone who loves the outdoors. Lasting roughly an hour, the trail takes you through lush green rainforest, where you will be welcomed by cheeky monkeys. Stay alert: you may also see zebras in the distance, several kinds of antelope grazing, or a solitary buffalo watching you with mild curiosity.

blocks.orig: Reaching the waterfall itself is the highlight of this tour. The sight of the water cascading down roughly 24 metres (80 feet) into a crystal-clear pool will make you gasp for the wonderfully fresh air. Fancy a cool(ing) shower? Go ahead, you’ve definitely deserved it!
blocks.html: The waterfall is the high point of the tour. Seeing the water plunge around 24 metres (80 feet) into a crystal-clear pool will leave you gasping for that wonderfully fresh air. Like a cool(ing) shower? Go on, you have certainly earned it!

blocks.orig: And if you decide to dine al fresco with a packed picnic, there’s no better backdrop than these majestic falls – simply breathe, relax, eat, repeat.
blocks.html: Should you choose to eat outdoors with a packed picnic, you won't find a finer setting than these majestic falls – just breathe, unwind, eat and do it all again.

blocks.orig: Take a Walking Safari in Arusha National Park
blocks.html: Go on a walking safari in Arusha National Park

blocks.orig: During this very special safari, you won’t hear the rumble of an engine, but nothing else than the sound of nature. Together with a guide, you’ll walk across the park and get close to animals like zebras, giraffes, different kinds of antelopes and the park’s famous black-and-white Colobus monkeys. Nice plus: your guide will also tell you more about the local flora and fun facts about the wildlife.
blocks.html: On this rather special safari, there is no engine noise, only the sounds of nature. With a guide at your side you walk through the park and come close to zebras, giraffes, several types of antelope and the well-known black-and-white colobus monkeys of the park. A nice bonus: your guide also shares background on the local plants and fun facts about the animals.

blocks.orig: The park is also home to the stunning Ngurdoto Crater, often referred to as the “Little Ngorongoro” – a true haven for a variety of four-legged and winged fellas due to its lush, verdant floor. Another highlight of the park are the Momela Lakes, offering a peaceful setting that contrasts with the wild landscapes around it. If you like birds – or the colour pink – this is your place to be, since countless flamingos have made these lakes their home.
blocks.html: In the park you will also find the beautiful Ngurdoto Crater, which people often call the “Little Ngorongoro” – thanks to its lush green floor, it is a real refuge for all kinds of creatures with four legs or wings. The Momela Lakes are another highlight, with a calm setting that stands out against the wild scenery around them. Do you love birds – or the colour pink? Then this is the place for you, as huge numbers of flamingos live on these lakes.

blocks.orig: Word of caution: Wildlife interactions in movies look a lot smoother than they are in real life, and the starring role in “I Petted a Lion (and Lived to Regret It)” surely isn’t on anyone’s bucket list 😉 Therefore, please follow the guide’s instructions to the tee. Thanks.
blocks.html: A word of warning: Encounters with wild animals look much smoother on screen than in reality, and nobody has the leading role in “I Petted a Lion (and Lived to Regret It)” on their bucket list 😉 So please do exactly what your guide tells you. Thank you.

blocks.orig: Let’s stay in Arusha National Park for a little while longer, because it’s oh-so-pretty! How about adding a splash of adventure to your trip with a canoe tour? On the serene waters of Momela Lakes, you can simply paddle your worries away. Here, you’ll feel a million miles away from the hubbub of the city as you take in the tranquil lake views, vibrant wildlife, and fresh mountain air.
blocks.html: Let’s linger in Arusha National Park a little longer, as it really is so lovely! Why not give your trip a dash of adventure by joining a canoe tour? Out on the calm water of the Momela Lakes, you can just paddle your cares away. The noise of the city will feel a world away while you enjoy the peaceful views across the lake, the lively wildlife and the fresh mountain air.

blocks.orig: Located just outside of Arusha, Mount Longido is a stunning 2,636 metres (8,651 ft) volcanic peak that offers incredible panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. For those looking for an invigorating day hike near Arusha, climbing Longido is a fantastic option. The hike up Longido takes most hikers around six hours. The trail starts off through lush forests before opening up to more rocky terrain. As you climb higher, you’ll be treated to sweeping vistas of Mount Meru, Namanga Hills, Ol Doinyo Lengai, and even Kilimanjaro, if the day is especially clear.
blocks.html: Just outside Arusha rises Mount Longido, a striking volcanic peak of 2,636 metres (8,651 ft) with superb panoramic views over the landscape around it. If you want a refreshing day hike close to Arusha, climbing Longido is an excellent choice. The climb up Longido takes most walkers about six hours. At first the path winds through lush forest, then it gives way to rockier ground. The higher you get, the wider the views over Mount Meru, the Namanga Hills, Ol Doinyo Lengai and, on a particularly clear day, even Kilimanjaro.

blocks.orig: Pro tip: climbing this mountain is no easy feat, so pack your determination alongside your gear.
blocks.html: Pro tip: this is not an easy mountain to climb, so bring plenty of determination along with your kit.

blocks.orig: The Tanzanite Museum in Arusha is a unique attraction that you definitely shouldn’t miss if you’re in the area. The museum houses an impressive collection of tanzanite gemstones which will make your eyes sparkle. Learn more about the history of this rare precious stone and see some of the world’s most beautiful examples up close. And if you’re smitten with the shiny stones, simply get your own piece of tanzanite jewellery at the museum’s gift shop.
blocks.html: If you are nearby, make sure you don't skip the Tanzanite Museum in Arusha, a one-of-a-kind attraction. Its remarkable collection of tanzanite gems will make your eyes light up. Discover the story of this rare precious stone and admire some of the finest examples in the world from close by. Fallen for the sparkling stones? Then just buy a tanzanite jewellery piece of your own in the museum gift shop.

blocks.orig: Enjoy Mountain Biking In and Near Arusha
blocks.html: Go mountain biking in and around Arusha

blocks.orig: Discover the area in and around Arusha on two wheels instead of four – and burn some calories while doing so! On a mountain bike, you can explore the region’s diverse terrains with breathtaking views and paths for different skill levels.
blocks.html: Explore Arusha and its surroundings on two wheels rather than four – and work off a few calories on the way! By mountain bike you can discover the varied terrain of the region, with stunning views and routes for every level of rider.

blocks.orig: Mount Meru, which caters to intermediate to advanced bikers with its forest tracks and wildlife sightings.
blocks.html: Mount Meru, with forest trails and wildlife sightings, suits intermediate and advanced riders.

blocks.orig: Arusha National Park, with its mix of natural dirt roads and forest paths, is ideal for wildlife enthusiasts of all biking levels.
blocks.html: Arusha National Park combines natural dirt tracks with forest trails, making it perfect for wildlife lovers of every cycling level.

blocks.orig: The cultural Usa River Trails passes through coffee plantations and local villages.
blocks.html: The cultural Usa River Trails take you through coffee plantations and local villages.

blocks.orig: Lake Duluti’s circular trail is perfect for beginners and bird watchers alike.
blocks.html: Lake Duluti’s loop trail suits novices and birdwatchers equally well.

blocks.orig: Did you know that Tanzania is famous for producing some of the best coffee beans in the world? Well, it does, and that’s why visiting the coffee fields in Arusha is a must-do. Learning all about how coffee is grown, harvested, and processed in Tanzania, makes this experience both educational and fun. While you get blown away by the beauty of the rolling hills covered in neat rows of coffee plants, your knowledgeable guide will tell you everything he knows about coffee farming. Of course, you’ll end this day with some freshly brewed coffee – enjoy!
blocks.html: Were you aware that Tanzania is known for growing some of the finest coffee beans on earth? It really is, which is why a visit to the coffee fields of Arusha should be on your list. Finding out how coffee is cultivated, picked and processed in Tanzania makes this outing both informative and enjoyable. As you take in the beauty of the rolling hills lined with tidy rows of coffee plants, your well-informed guide shares all he knows about growing coffee. Naturally, the day finishes with a cup of freshly brewed coffee – enjoy!

blocks.orig: Check Out Meserani Snake Park and Maasai Museum
blocks.html: Visit the Meserani Snake Park and Maasai Museum

blocks.orig: The Meserani Snake Park is a fun family activity with educational shows for the kids… and grown-ups. It’s home to various species of snakes, like puff adders, green and black mambas, and the Egyptian cobra, as well as crocodiles, lizards, and, oddly enough, birds.
blocks.html: The Meserani Snake Park makes an enjoyable family outing, with informative shows for children… and adults. You will find many kinds of snakes there, including puff adders, green and black mambas and the Egyptian cobra, plus crocodiles, lizards and, strangely, birds.

blocks.orig: The cultural Boma onsite features the Maasai Museum, which displays traditional artefacts. Here you can learn about the semi-nomadic Maasai tribe’s customs and culture. Traditional weapons, beads, gourds, and everyday objects give you an inside look at the lifestyle of these fascinating indigenous people. This is a great cultural experience, you don’t want to miss.
blocks.html: At the cultural Boma on site is the Maasai Museum, where traditional artefacts are on display. It teaches you about the customs and culture of the semi-nomadic Maasai people. Through traditional weapons, beadwork, gourds and everyday items, you get a close look at how these fascinating indigenous people live. It is a wonderful cultural experience that you should not miss.

blocks.orig: Arusha is home to many fascinating sights and historical landmarks that are worth exploring on a guided city tour. Taking a half-day or full-day city tour is a great way to see the best the city has to offer in a short amount of time. And the best thing: you don’t have to worry about navigating or planning the best route. Just soak up the atmosphere, stories, and scenery. Done.
blocks.html: Arusha has lots of interesting sights and historic landmarks that are well worth discovering on a guided tour of the city. A half-day or full-day city tour lets you see the highlights of Arusha in little time. Best of all, you need not think about directions or the best route. Simply take in the atmosphere, the stories and the views. That's it.

blocks.orig: The Arusha Maasai Market is a famous spot to buy a souvenir for your loved ones – or yourself. Located near the clock tower in central Arusha, this market is open seven days a week and brings together artisans and craftspeople selling traditional Maasai pieces. At the market, bargaining is both welcomed and expected. Don’t be shy to negotiate prices on items that catch your eye. With good-natured haggling and a smile, you’re likely to get the best deals.
blocks.html: If you want a souvenir for family and friends – or for yourself – the Arusha Maasai Market is a well-known place to go. Close to the clock tower in the centre of Arusha, the market is open every day of the week and gathers artisans and craftspeople who sell traditional Maasai goods. Haggling is welcome here, and in fact expected. Feel free to negotiate the price of anything you like. Bargain with good humour and a smile, and you will probably get the best price.

blocks.html: Colourful Maasai beadwork jewellery, which often uses colours and symbols with cultural meaning.

blocks.html: Carvings of wild animals and Maasai warriors, made from local wood such as ebony.

blocks.orig: Hand-dyed, loosely woven shukas and other textiles in vivid colours.
blocks.html: Shukas and other loosely woven, hand-dyed fabrics in bright colours.

blocks.orig: Getting around this vibrant city and its surroundings is half the fun. With stunning scenery abound, travelling between each adventure will be a sightseeing experience in itself.
blocks.html: Half the fun lies in getting around this lively city and the area around it. With so much beautiful scenery, the journey between each adventure becomes a sightseeing trip of its own.

blocks.orig: Get a glimpse into local life and culture as you hop aboard one of Arusha’s colourful (and mostly crowded) buses or shared minivans, called dala dalas. While routes and schedules can be confusing for newbies, fares are extremely cheap, and you’ll get to chat with friendly locals – how’s that for authentic?
blocks.html: Catch a glimpse of everyday life and culture by jumping on one of the colourful (and usually packed) buses or shared minibuses of Arusha, known as dala dalas. The routes and timetables may baffle first-timers, but tickets cost very little and you can chat with friendly locals – what could be more authentic?

blocks.orig: Nothing beats the freedom of having your own set of 4×4 wheels in Arusha. Splurge on a rental car or 4WD vehicle to journey on your own schedule. Driving yourself allows you to venture to more remote areas and discover hidden gems at your own pace. Just be ready for bumpy, unpaved roads and be sure to know some basic car repair skills, e. g. changing a tyre.
blocks.html: Nothing compares with the freedom of your own 4×4 in Arusha. Treat yourself to a hire car or 4WD vehicle so you can travel on your own timetable. Behind the wheel yourself, you can head to more remote places and find hidden gems at your own speed. Just be prepared for rough, unsealed roads and make sure you have some basic car repair skills, such as changing a tyre.
